decisive_items: a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias
KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R identified as the only somatic mutation
response.rationale: The clinical description and histopathological findings of a blanchable red plaque with telangiectasias, combined with the genetic finding of a KDR (VEGFR2) mutation, support the diagnosis of Telangiectasia. The absence of pain, pruritus, or epidermal abnormality further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.why: Lack of direct clinical or histopathological evidence to support Cutaneous Collateral Vessel Formation
While the clinical presentation is consistent with Cutaneous Angiokeratoma, the histopathological findings and genetic mutation are more specific to Telangiectasia

The presence of small-caliber vessels and blanchable red plaque could suggest Angiosarcoma, but the lack of malignant features and the specific genetic mutation identified make Telangiectasia a more likely diagnosis
While the lesion is described as solitary, this is a modifier of the champion diagnosis, Telangiectasia, rather than a distinct diagnosis
